tool: Ghidra 12.1 (pyghidra 3.x via tools/ghidra/scripts/{list_functions,decompile}.py; list_functions.py fixed to use open_project/program_context). ega.drv already imported by setup.sh (BinaryLoader, x86:LE:16 Real Mode, base seg 0 -> Ghidra address == file offset).
summary: Static-RE of the ega.drv blit service that wmaze-render-in-egadrv.json located dynamically. ega.drv is a DOS graphics driver with a 17-entry far-call dispatch table at file 0x00 (e9 jmp, then `e8 rel16; cb retf` thunks at 0x03,0x07,...,0x43). **Entry 10 (offset 0x2b) -> handler FUN_1c94 (file 0x1c94, 1144 bytes) is the wall/sprite COMPOSITOR** -- it contains the EGA planar span writer at file 0x2069 (es=A000, dx=0x3c5 Sequencer) that the dynamic trace caught at lin 0x6c219. FUN_1c94 clears a 0x1400-byte compose buffer to 0xff (all-planes-set = transparent), reads tile (width,height) from a 0x18-stride descriptor table indexed by (pieceString[0]-1), loops the piece-index string calling FUN_210c per piece, then applies optional palette-remap (flag bit0, LUT at +0x192), horizontal flip (flag bit1, 8-wide byte-swap), clipping (args +0xc/+0x10), and the planar blit to VRAM. FUN_210c (file 0x210c) is the per-piece MASKED 4-PLANE EGA BLIT: pixels are EGA planar (4 planes at src[0]/[8]/[0x10]/[0x18], cell stride 0x20); transparency = AND of all 4 planes (transp = p0&p1&p2&p3); merge = dst = src&~transp | dst&transp; a per-cell presence bitmap (descriptor+2, rotating bit mask) selects which cells are emitted; flags give H/V flip. This is the 'proprietary masked blob' the prior wmaze passes could not decode -- it is standard 4-plane EGA masked sprite data, NOT a custom format and NOT 2bpp (corrects the '2bpp' guess in wmaze-render-in-egadrv.json#twobpp-column-writer; the rotating bx/dx masks seen in the trace are the EGA plane/bit masks).

findings.claim: ega.drv exposes a 17-entry far-call dispatch table at file 0x00: `e9 00 00` (jmp self+3) then 17x `e8 rel16; cb` (near-call handler; far-return). Callers far-call ega_seg:offset (0x03,0x07,...,0x43). Handlers: e0->0x19a, e1->0x43a, e2->0x55f, e3->0xeae, e4->0xf0a, e5->0xff7, e6->0xfe1, e7->0xfab, e8->0xd2f, e9->0x1c25, **e10(off 0x2b)->0x1c94**, e11->0x5f0, e12->0x631, e13->0x735, e14->0x7b3, e15->0xa93, e16->0x192e.

evidence.details: Header bytes: e9 00 00 e8 94 01 cb e8 30 04 cb e8 51 05 cb ... Decoded e8 rel16 (target = addr_after+rel) for all 17 thunks; each followed by cb (retf). Entry 10 @0x2b -> 0x1c94 is the largest handler and contains the traced planar writer (file 0x2069 = lin 0x6c219).

findings.claim: FUN_1c94 (entry 10) is the wall/sprite compositor + VRAM blit. Decompiled behavior: (1) clear a 0x1400-byte compose buffer to 0xff (transparent); (2) tile (w,h) = descriptorTable[(pieceString[0]-1)*0x18 + 2/+3]; (3) for each byte in the piece-index string (arg @+0x18) call FUN_210c (decode+merge that piece into the buffer); (4) if flag(+0x14)&1: palette-remap every buffer byte through LUT at +0x192; (5) if flag&2: horizontal-flip (swap bytes [0]<->[7],[1]<->[6],[2]<->[5],[3]<->[4] across 8-wide cells); (6) clip using args +0xc (start) / +0x10 (end); (7) planar blit to A000 via the writer at file 0x2069. Args (near-cdecl, bp+): +0x0a tile/col index (into table @0x17a), +0x0c/+0x10 clip bounds, +0x14 flags, +0x18 piece-index string ptr.

evidence.details: FUN_0000_1c94 decompile: `for(iVar10=0x1400;...) *p++=0xff;` then `iVar10=(byte)(*arg18-1)*0x18; w=*(iVar10+2); h=*(iVar10+3);` then `while(*arg18) { FUN_210c(); arg18++; }` then `if(flags&1){ b=LUT[b+0x192] }` then `if(flags&2){ 8-wide byte-swap }` then clip via (+0x10 - +0xc). The planar writer at 0x2069 (es=A000, dx=0x3c5) is inside this function (dynamic trace lin 0x6c219, 805 hits, di stride 0x28).

findings.claim: FUN_210c is the per-piece masked 4-plane EGA blit (the texture/sprite decoder). Pixels are EGA planar: a cell is 4 planes at src offsets [0],[8],[0x10],[0x18], cell stride 0x20. Transparency mask = AND of the 4 planes (transp = p0 & p1 & p2 & p3). Per-plane merge: dst[p] = src[p] & ~transp | dst[p] & transp. A per-row presence bitmap (descriptor+2, a rotating bit `bVar7` from 1, left-rotating each cell) selects which cells are emitted vs skipped (advance dst by 0x20). H-flip (flag bit0): src/dst offset (w-1)*0x20, step backward. V-flip (flag bit1): start offset w*0x20*(h-1).

evidence.details: FUN_0000_210c decompile inner cell loop: `bVar7 = src[0]&src[8]&src[0x10]&src[0x18]; bVar8 = ~bVar7; dst[0]=src[0]&bVar8|dst[0]&bVar7; dst[8]=...; dst[0x10]=...; dst[0x18]=...;` 8 iterations (8 columns) per cell, advancing src+1/dst+1; then src+=0x19, dst+=0x19. Outer loop walks a presence bitmap (`if((*mask & bit)==0) skip cell (dst+=0x20)`), bit rotates left, advancing mask ptr when it wraps. descriptor = (pieceIdx-1)*0x18; descriptor[0]=src ptr, descriptor+2 = mask bytes. Confirms: 4-plane EGA, all-planes-set = transparent.

findings.claim: The dynamic-trace 'render-only' addresses past ega.drv's 0x2262 file image (lin 0x6c552, 0x6d9e0) are the COMPOSE BUFFER region (segment ~0x4182 / the 0x1400-byte buffer FUN_1c94 clears), NOT separate code. At idle the region holds stale 4-plane pixel bytes (capstone of an idle dump there = garbage/data: 0x80-0x8c runs). The blit code itself is the in-image FUN_1c94/FUN_210c; the trace caught the CPU writing/reading the buffer during compose. (Open: re-confirm whether any blit inner loop is genuinely runtime-relocated vs simply operating on the buffer -- the in-image decompile fully explains the behavior, so the port does NOT need the transient buffer bytes.)

evidence.details: Idle dump /tmp/wiz6-seg6b91.bin at dump+0xc42 (lin 0x6c552) and +0x20d0 (lin 0x6d9e0) capstone-disassembles to incoherent ops over byte runs 0x80/0x84/0x88/0x8c (= EGA pixel shades), i.e. data not code AT FRAME BOUNDARIES. RESOLVED below by the capture tooling: the region is a WORK BUFFER into which ega.drv COPIES a blit template (file 0x1fd0) and executes it mid-frame; by the boundary it holds pixel data again.

findings.claim: The live corridor WALL rasterizer, captured mid-frame via the new capture-on-breakpoint tooling, is an EGA PLANAR PIXEL read-modify-write blitter. Its code is ega.drv file 0x1fd0 (inside the FUN_1c94 region) COPIED into a work buffer (~lin 0x6d800) and executed there (which is why file-address tracing never caught it). Per pixel-group it: reads source texture bytes (ds:si+8, si+0x10, ... = the 4 EGA planes, stride 8), shr by cl (column alignment), AND with bx (set-mask), merges into dest with `dst=(dst&dx_clearmask)|(src&bx_setmask)`, then if flag [bp+0x18]&1 writes to A000 VRAM via the EGA Sequencer Map Mask (port 0x3c5 reg 2) + Graphics Controller (0x3cf) + latched read/write (mov al,es:[di]; mov es:[di],al); else writes to the off-screen page at es:[di+0x2000]. So the maze view composes to an off-screen page (+0x2000) OR straight to VRAM depending on the flag.

evidence.details: Captured with `trace-maze.ts cap 6d9e0 6d800 1000 0`: live mid-frame bytes differ from the idle view in 4064/4096 bytes (confirming the boundary view is stale data). Capstone of the capture @0x6d9e0: `mov ah,[si+8]; shr ax,cl; and ax,bx; xchg al,ah; mov [bp-0xa],ax; mov ax,es:[di+0x2000]; and ax,dx; or ax,[bp-0xa]; test [bp+0x18],1; je +; <push es/dx/ax; mov dx,3c5; mov al,2; out dx,al; mov dx,3cf; out dx,al; mov ax,a000; mov es,ax; mov al,es:[di]; pop ax; mov es:[di],al; ...>; mov ax,es:[di+0x2000]` (off-screen path). The code signature `8a 64 08 d3 e8 23 c3 86 e0` is found in ega.drv @ file 0x1fd0 -> the template is in-image (Ghidra-analyzable), executed from a copy at lin 0x6d800+.

findings.claim: Full wall-rasterizer algorithm (4-plane EGA, captured + disassembled). The executed blob is a VERBATIM copy of ega.drv file 0x1df0..0x2262 (0 byte diffs over 0x472 bytes) into a work buffer; entered for the per-column blit at the offset == file 0x1fd0. OUTER loop (file 0x1df0..0x1fd0): loads the work segment from cs:[0x16d] into ds/es; computes a row stride [bp-8] = ([bp-2]-1)<<5 (32 bytes = a 4-plane*8 cell); builds per-column edge masks from the sub-byte position (cx=[bp-6]&7; setmask ah=0xff<<cl, clearmask al=~ah -> [bp-0xc]); clears/initializes column strips (rep stosw 0xffff = transparent, or and/or with the edge mask over 0x20-byte rows); clips against Y bounds [bp+0xe] (top) / [bp+0x14] (bottom). INNER per-plane block (0x1fd0, x4 unrolled, source planes at si+0/+8/+0x10/+0x18, stride 8): ah=src plane byte; shr ax,cl (column align); and ax,bx (valid-pixel set-mask); merge dst=(dst & dx_clearmask) | (src & bx); write to the off-screen PLANAR page es:[di + 0x2000*plane] (plane stride 0x2000) OR, if [bp+0x18]&1, straight to A000 VRAM via Sequencer Map Mask (out 0x3c5, plane-bit 1/2/4/8) + GC (0x3cf) + latched read/write. So the maze composes into a 4-plane off-screen page (4*0x2000=0x8000), then (elsewhere) blits to VRAM.

evidence.details: Capture /tmp/wiz6-wallrast.bin (base lin 0x6d800 == ega.drv file 0x1df0) == ega.drv[0x1df0:0x2262] byte-exact (0 diffs). Capstone of the outer loop @0x6d802: `mov ax,[bp-2]; dec ax; mov cl,5; shl ax,cl; mov [bp-8],ax` (row stride (w-1)*32); `mov ax,cs:[0x16d]; mov ds,ax` (work seg); edge-mask build @0x6d8a4 `mov cx,[bp-6]; and cx,7; mov ah,0xff; shl ah,cl; mov al,ah; not al; mov [bp-0xc],ax`; clip @0x6d834 `shl ax,3; add ax,[bp+0xe]; cmp ax,[bp+0x14]`. Inner 4-plane block @0x6d9e0/0x6da31/0x6da82/... at source si+8/+0x10/+0x18 with off-screen dest +0x2000/+0x4000/+0x6000 and VRAM-vs-offscreen branch on [bp+0x18]&1.

findings.claim: DECODER-FIRST RESULT: the corridor texture format is authoritatively confirmed from the asm. The fresh-load corridor blit @ lin 0x6dbd5 was captured live (capture-on-breakpoint during the LOAD compose) and disassembled — it is the SAME 4-plane MASKED MERGE as FUN_210c (the earlier register-trace 'byte copy' read was wrong). Exact loop: `cx=8; bl=[si]&[si+8]&[si+0x10]&[si+0x18] (transp=AND of 4 planes); bh=bl; bl=~bl; for each plane P in {0,8,0x10,0x18}: es:[di+P] = ([si+P]&bl) | (es:[di+P]&bh); si++; di++; loop; si+=0x18; di+=0x18`. So the TEXTURE FORMAT is: 8x8-pixel tiles, 4-plane EGA (1 bit/plane/px), 0x20 bytes/tile, plane p = tile[p*8 .. p*8+7] (8 rows), transparency = pixels where all 4 planes are set, merge = src over dst by transparency. This fully grounds the prior 'masked blob' mystery in asm. REMAINING (data-side, NOT format) — DEEPER THAN DECODE-GUESSING: 6 decode attempts (source 0x550e0 + compose page 0x6a0f0; row-major + column-major; widths 11/16/22/40) ALL yielded noise. Structural reason: the compose page (0x6a0f0) is an INTERMEDIATE that the planar writer (lin 0x6c219 / ega.drv@0x2069) further transforms to VRAM with PER-COLUMN SHIFTS (`shr ax,cl` — this is where the convergence lives), so the compose page is NOT laid out as the screen and no flat tile-grid decode of it can match the framebuffer; and the raw source asset is likely COMPRESSED (0x550e0 is a working buffer, ~81% zero). So the data-side needs a dedicated deeper pass: (a) reverse the planar-writer compose->VRAM transform (the shr/mask/di-stride geometry) to map compose tiles -> screen, and (b) locate + decode the clean texture asset (decompression). This is beyond decode-guessing; do NOT keep guessing tile layouts.

evidence.details: capload phase: traceSet(0x6dbd5) + captureSet during the dungeon LOAD render -> /tmp/wiz6-blitcode.bin. Capstone @0x6dbd5: `mov cx,8; mov bl,[si]; and bl,[si+8]; and bl,[si+0x10]; and bl,[si+0x18]; mov bh,bl; not bl; mov al,[si]; and al,bl; mov ah,es:[di]; and ah,bh; or al,ah; mov es:[di],al; <repeat for +8,+0x10,+0x18>; inc si; inc di; loop; add si,0x18; add di,0x18`. Matches FUN_210c's inner cell loop exactly. The 4-plane decode of /tmp/wiz6-maze-tex.bin (8x8 tiles) produced noise -> data-location issue, not format.

findings.claim: FRESH-LOAD render anatomy (via memory-write-watch + trace during the initial dungeon LOAD — the FULL texture compose runs at load, NOT on per-step redraws, which is why earlier per-step traces missed it). NOTE: work-buffer/compose/texture addresses at fresh load DIFFER from the unserialize(CLEAN_STATE) layout (heap-dependent), so addresses below are fresh-load-specific. (1) COMPOSE PAGE = segment 0x6a0f (linear 0x6a0f0), spanning ~0x6a0f0..0x6b500 — the off-screen 3D view buffer (NOT seg 0x4182, which was the unserialize layout). (2) BUFFER-CLEAR loop @ lin 0x6d6c0: rep-stosw of ax=0xff into es=0x6a0f, cx counts down from 0x1400 (=5120, the FUN_1c94 clear-to-transparent step). (3) TEXTURE CELL BLIT @ lin 0x6dbd5/0x6dbe5/0x6dbf6/0x6dc07 (4 cseips = the 4 EGA planes): ds=0x550e:si (the SOURCE TEXTURE, linear 0x550e0) -> es=0x6a0f:di (compose page); inner loop cx=8 (8 px/row), si and di both +1 inner then both +0x20 per row -> a 1:1 8-wide cell copy with 0x20 source/dest stride, NO per-pixel perspective scaling. So the perspective/convergence is entirely in the OUTER driver's per-cell (si,di) selection (which source cell maps to which screen cell), not the inner blit.

evidence.details: wwload (write-watch 0x60000..0x90000 during dungeon LOAD): top writers all in the work buffer 0x6d6c0..0x6dc07 writing the compose page 0x6a0f0..0x6b4ef. drvtrace of 0x6d6c0: es=6a0f, ax=ff, cx=1400 countdown, di sweeps the page = clear loop. drvtrace of 0x6dbd5 during LOAD compose: ds=550e si steps 0x1a78,0x1a79..0x1a7f (8) then 0x1a98 (+0x20); di 0xbe0..0xbe7 then 0xc00 (+0x20); ax = source texel byte (0x18,0x3,0,0x20,0x38..); cx 8..1. si/di lockstep => 1:1 cell copy. Source texture seg ds=0x550e (linear 0x550e0); compose page es=0x6a0f (0x6a0f0).

caveat_for_prior_findings: Refines wmaze-render-in-egadrv.json AND this file's own earlier conclusion: ega.drv IS the graphics service far-called from wmaze, and the planar writer (0x2069) DOES blit the corridor to A000 every frame. The wall rasterizer is a separate compiled/transient code path (0x6c400-0x6e400) that frame-granular tooling cannot capture. The 4-plane masked format is correct and portable for sprites. Earlier '2bpp column writer' wording is retired.
